narrative.overview: StoreFlow is an operating surface, not a showcase. Its world is the shop's own paper ledger: a warm off-white ground the colour of a receipt, near-black ink for anything the owner must read precisely, and a single deep petrol accent that appears only where the interface asks for a decision. Density is the discipline here - management screens run compact (32 px rows, 8 px spacing rhythm) so a thousand SKUs are scannable; the point-of-sale screen runs generous (44 px hit targets, a 34 px grand total) so a standing cashier reads it under shop lighting without a mouse. The interface is bilingual by construction rather than by a translation pass, so right-to-left is a first-class layout mode, not a mirror applied at the end. Nothing asks the user to translate meaning: status is always carried by an icon and a word as well as a colour, and every error states the next action instead of reporting a fault.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, near-black ink, one deep petrol accent used sparingly.
Zero literal colour in view code - every colour is a semantic role resolved at runtime.
Compact management tables, generous point-of-sale targets, one density token family.
Status always carries an icon and a text label; colour never carries meaning alone.
Tabular figures in every money and quantity column, in both scripts.
Right-to-left is a layout mode, not a cosmetic flip.

rules.name: The Semantic-Only Rule
rules.body: A view may never contain a literal colour. Every colour in the product is a semantic role that the theme file fills in.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Petrol covers no more than roughly a tenth of any screen. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The State Carries a Word Rule
rules.body: No state is communicated by colour alone. Every badge pairs its colour with an icon and a text label.

rules.name: The Ring Is Visible Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is always drawn as a 2 px petrol ring offset 3 px outside the control, never removed, never the only difference between focus and hover.

rules.name: The Scale Multiplies Rule
rules.body: Typography scale is a single multiplier in the theme file applied to 12 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 28 / 34 px. No screen carries its own font size.

rules.name: The Arabic Leads Rule
rules.body: Arabic sets with roughly 1.6x the Latin leading, and always with TextOptions.TextFormattingMode=Display - Ideal breaks the ligatures.

rules.name: The Figure Alignment Rule
rules.body: Any column of money, quantity, or percentage uses tabular figures and right alignment.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Separation comes from tone and a hairline rule, never from a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Border Means Pressable Rule
rules.body: A control with a visible rule-strong border is interactive; a container with a rule-subtle border is not. The two are never mixed.

dos: Do reference a semantic role for every colour, in every view.
Do pair every status colour with an icon and a word.
Do use the 8 px spacing rhythm and the density tokens rather than ad-hoc margins.
Do set tabular figures and right alignment on every money and quantity column.
Do render Arabic with TextOptions.TextFormattingMode=Display and mirror the shell through FlowDirection.
Do keep the primary accent to one action per screen.
Do draw the focus ring on every focusable control, including custom ones.
Do add a new semantic role to the theme schema before using a new colour anywhere.
donts: Don't put a literal colour in a view, a control template, or a converter.
Don't introduce a shadow, a gradient, a glass effect, or a glow.
Don't communicate state with colour alone, and don't rely on hover as the only affordance.
Don't mirror a logo or a non-directional icon under right-to-left.
Don't put a SKU, barcode, phone number, or email inside an Arabic sentence without isolating it.
Don't hard-code a font size in a view - change the theme scale instead.
Don't show a raw exception string; state the condition and the next action in the user's language.
Don't round money for display twice - format from minor units once.
